articles.title: Guardian-produced Gaza documentary from Oscar-winning Israeli directors of No Other Land to screen at Venice film festival
articles.summary: Film directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, co-directors of No Other Land along with Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, investigates ‘Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians’ during the war.
body: A new documentary about Israel’s bombing campaign in Gaza, directed by Oscar-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, is to receive its world premiere at the Venice film festival.

The film, called NAZA, has been produced with Jim Wilson and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer, the team behind The Zone of Interest, and is the only documentary that will compete this year for Venice’s prestigious Golden Lion.
Abraham and Szor are the two Israeli directors of the four behind No Other Land, which won the Oscar for best documentary in 2025.

Announcing the news, the film-makers said: “Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.”

articles.title: Post your questions for Alex Winter
articles.summary: The 80s icon and star of The Lost Boys and Bill & Ted has also had a storied career behind the camera and on stage. Now, he’ll answer your (non-bogus) questions. You probably still think of Alex Winter as Kiefer Sutherland’s bloodsucking, peroxide-haired vampire biker mate Marko in 1987’s The Lost…
body: But Winter actually started out as a child actor on Broadway, appearing in The King and I with Yul Brynner before making his big-screen debut opposite Charles Bronson in 1985’s Death Wish 3. As well as the above, he played poet and physician John William Polidori in 1988’s Haunted Summer, and co-wrote, co-directed and starred in the 1993 cult comedy Freaked.

Since then, Winter has mainly been behind the camera: he wrote and directed the well-received psychological thriller Fever, starring ET the Extra-Terrestrial’s Henry Thomas, in 1999, and has made documentaries on everything from the dark web to child stardom and Frank Zappa. In 2020, he reunited with his old buddy Reeves for a third Bill & Ted film; and then reunited with him again in 2025, playing Vladimir opposite Reeves’s Estragon in Waiting for Godot on Broadway.

articles.title: The Visitor review – existential Lithuania-set homecoming drama leaves everything in limbo
articles.summary: This portrait by Vytautas Katkus of a man contemplating his recent fatherhood and his own father is steeped in ennui and ends up drifting. At one point in this Nordic-Baltic homecoming film, Danielius (Darius Šilėnas) refuses an invite for beachfront karaoke, preferring to watch from behind a…
body: Little tangible is disclosed. Danielius is a thirtysomething father who skipped the funeral of his own dad the year before. Preparing the flat to go on the market, he walks the dog of his neighbour, Vismante (Vismantė Ruzgaitė), hangs speculatively at beach gatherings and falls asleep in pine forests. Ice-cream is eaten at every available opportunity. He’s not alienated exactly, but somewhat out of step. As he looks for new anchorage, even the film seems to question whether Danielius has sufficient main character energy: it periodically drifts to follow another resident, Tomas (Rokas Siaurusaitis), who is caring for his grandmother over the way.

articles.title: WildBrain Acquires ‘Kid Safe’ Generative-AI Platform Personality AI in Deal Worth up to $69 Million
articles.summary: WildBrain, the Canadian children’s media company with the rights to titles such as “Yo Gabba Gabba!” and the “Teletubbies,” has purchased the child-focused generative AI startup Personality AI in a cash-and-stock deal worth up to $69 million in a bid to marry the company’s intellectual property…
body: “Personality AI enables more continuous interaction between fans and brands, strengthening our ability to deliver end-to-end franchise solutions to partners,” WildBrain CEO and president Josh Sceherba said in a statement. “This highly complementary acquisition positions us and Personality AI as a more integrated partner to IP owners globally through our in-house licensing agency, WildBrain CPLG, while helping support the continued growth of both our owned and partner brands.”

Wildbrain paid roughly $11 million in cash along with 1 million shares. Shareholders will also receive $2 million worth of WildBrain shares (up to 1 million shares) in additional consideration on the first anniversary of closing, with the remaining balance paid in cash. The deal also includes up to $56 million in performance-based cash consideration based on Personality AI’s revenue performance between 2027 and 2029. Personality CEO John Goscha will join WildBrain as the executive vice president for Personality AI and will report to Scherba.

articles.title: ESPN to Hike Prices of Streaming Plans Next Month
articles.summary: ESPN is ratcheting up the price of its streaming services — just in time for the busy fall sports season. Effective Sept. 17, the Disney-owned sports giant is increasing the monthly and annual pricing for both ESPN Unlimited and the scaled-down ESPN Select tier.
body: ESPN Select is going from $12.99 to $13.99/month, while the annual plan is increasing from $129.99 to $139.99/year. ESPN Select provides some 32,000 live events annually but does not include access to the ESPN linear networks.
In an Aug. 20 memo to ESPN staffers reviewed by Variety, chairman Jimmy Pitaro praised the team that launched the stand-alone streaming service a year ago.

“From the beginning, we set out to provide sports fans with optionality and a new way to connect with ESPN. Early on, we have delivered,” Pitaro wrote. “To everyone across ESPN and Disney who continues to work tirelessly to build this platform — thank you. While we’re still in the early innings of our direct-to-consumer journey, one year after the launch of ESPN DTC, we move forward with absolute confidence in where we are headed.”

articles.title: Marching in the Dark review – rural Indian widows show stunning resilience as they battle poverty and taboos
articles.summary: Kinshuk Surjan’s documentary follows women in dire financial straits whose bereavement compounds their social plight, which they confront together. Out in rural India, a crisis casts a dark cloud over the seemingly tranquil vistas of wheat fields and soy farms.
body: Sanjivani, a woman in her 30s, is one such case. Eight years after her husband killed himself, she has taken over some of the farming responsibilities, along with other odd jobs, to provide for her two children. The camera rarely finds her at rest; Sanjivani not only works in the fields but also performs domestic labour for her extended family – cooking, cleaning and doing laundry. Her resilience is stunning to witness, but even more impressive is the emotional support provided by a tight-knit network of other widows. Together, the women gather for counselling sessions where they can freely discuss their emotional, physical and financial issues.

articles.title: Rosie O’Donnell Should Host Her Own Show on Late-Night TV — and Shatter Comedy’s Greatest Glass Ceiling
articles.summary: Late night is in the doldrums. It’s not just that the remaining hosts are taking much of the summer off. But, post-Stephen Colbert on CBS, ABC’s Jimmy Kimmel and NBC’s Jimmy Fallon both feel closer to the end of their respective tenures than the beginning.
body: It’s been almost 40 years since Joan Rivers tried to break into the late-night boys’ club — and got fired by Fox after a single season. O’Donnell’s hiring as a woman at a flagship late-night show would break further ground — but would also bring in someone who totally reveres television and knows how to make it well. A form of TV that seems close to dying could use a jolt of energy, and O’Donnell, with her built-in fanbase and her ability to connect with, and provoke, audiences, might just be late night’s future.

On “Hacks,” as in our world, late night looks like a glass cliff for women — the field is shrinking, with CBS now out of the game entirely, just in time for a woman to potentially get called up. And yet, O’Donnell didn’t seem to mind, and hit the ground running on “Kimmel.” The female late-night hosts of recent vintage, CBS’ Taylor Tomlinson and NBC’s Lilly Singh, have seemed limited by both buried-in-the-evening time slot and by relatively low name recognition. O’Donnell’s hiring would be a moment that would electrify late night, drawing in an underserved audience of women and gay men and generating reams of press.

articles.title: EsDeeKid mystery no problem for fans after 'insane' All Points East set
articles.summary: We still don't know the Scouse rapper's true identity, but do music lovers really care who he is?
body: There might be fewer people guessing who he is these days - but if EsDeeKid's only UK festival appearance this summer is anything to go by, no-one seems to care.
The masked rapper took to the All Points East stage on Sunday night, reeling off his signature raw and punchy bars from on top of a castle.
When EsDeeKid, who raps with a Scouse accent and only ever reveals his eyes, burst on to the scene last year everyone was convinced he was Timothée Chalamet.
But the US actor finally shot those rumours down in December by performing alongside him in a new video.

articles.title: Dutch broadcaster Avrotros pulls out of 2027 Eurovision Song Contest
articles.summary: It says contest can no longer be considered neutral while a participating country remains involved in a large-scale military conflict.
body: In a statement, external released on Monday, the broadcaster said the decision was due to a lack of clarity from organisers - the Eurovision Broadcasting Union (EBU) - over assessing which countries could compete.

Avrotros added: "The severe humanitarian suffering in Gaza and the ongoing restrictions on press freedom have contributed to increasing divisions surrounding the Eurovision Song Contest in recent years."

Earlier this month, the EBU updated its rules to state that if a country involved in an armed conflict wins the competition, it will be ineligible to host it the following year. But Avrotros said those changes "do not provide sufficient confidence that ‌the ⁠independent and neutral character of the Eurovision Song Contest has been restored".
The broadcaster's withdrawal from next year's contest in Burgas, Bulgaria, does not necessarily rule out Dutch participation.

articles.title: Regal Launches Rewards+ Loyalty Program Amid Company’s Record-Setting Summer (Exclusive)
articles.summary: "This was an amazing summer," the theater chain's head of marketing Vikki Neil tells The Hollywood Reporter as it adds a new membership tier.
body: Regal Entertainment Group is expanding its loyalty program offerings as the movie theater chain enjoys a historic summer.

Rewards+ is the newest loyalty tier, following the free-to-join Regal Rewards that offers points and incentives on purchases, and Regal Unlimited, which is geared toward offering unlimited 2D movies and extra savings for the most frequent moviegoers. The company will also enhance the Unlimited experience with 200 points per $1 spent and double the credits for concessions and additional ticket purchases.

“We’ve had our free loyalty program, which had been around for 25 years, and then we’ve had Unlimited for several years now,” Regal head of marketing Vikki Neil tells THR. “But we really didn’t have something that spoke to people that want to go to the movies on a regular basis, but maybe aren’t going to go 10 times per month. We felt like there was a big opportunity in the market, and so this is really about giving people that opportunity to have that subscription offering that gives them something predictable. They know what their rate is, and it’s value-focused. It really targets, in my opinion, more families and younger people.”
